pr_title: c8d: Better handling of partially filled `AuthConfig`
pr_body:
### c8d/authorizer: Default to docker.io

When the `ServerAddress` in the `AuthConfig` provided by the client is empty, default to the default registry (registry-1.docker.io).

This makes the behaviour the same as with the containerd image store integration disabled.

https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/e58c267d66cd9c8fc89c582047b22158c9d44db8/registry/service.go#L67-L69

This fixes an issue where Docker Desktop users couldn't pull private images when using credentials provided by the Docker Desktop credential helper (without `docker login`).

### c8d: Don't create authorizer for empty AuthConfig
- Fixes: https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/45397

Don't create an authorizer just to return empty credentials and log warning about registry host not matching the (empty) host from auth config.


**- Description for the changelog**

**- A picture of a cute animal (not mandatory but encouraged)**

comments:
authConfig will be empty if no matching AuthConfig was found (user didn't login to the repository of that image).
The fix would be printing the warning only if cfgHost is not empty.

review_comments:
Given that `AuthConfig` here is a static username/password, and `authorizationCredsFromAuthConfig` effectively is filtering "does this match the host I'm connecting to?" I'm even wondering if this code should do the matching, and only set `Authorizer` if it matches the `optAuthConfig`'s `ServerAddress` 🤔 

(in practice, it _shouldn't_ matter, although it could (I guess) prevent some warnings 🤔)

Yeah, I was also thinking about that. On the other hand, since this function call is done in containerd, so we don't fully control when it's called, it felt appropriate to be a little bit more defensive than to potentially leak the credentials.
